patch.value: GH-1713: strict create offers no auditable deferred value, so importers cannot create an item whose deadline, assignee or acceptance criteria are not known yet

GH-1713 (filed 2026-11-12). Under the strict preset, strict create requires concrete values for deadline, assignee and acceptance criteria and refuses every way of saying a value is not known yet: the repeatable options accept an explicit clear, but the three required scalars refuse --unset and accept no deferred value. An importer that mirrors records from another system (pm-github gated issue sync, Linear, ADO or CSV importers) must either fail or invent a deadline and an assignee. pm-github runs its sync inside one atomic import, so in a strict tracker every new GitHub issue fails strict create and the whole daily sync rolls back; one fleet repository has failed this way on every run for 19 days (importer side tracked in unbraind/pm-github issue 237). Proposed direction from the issue: an explicit, auditable deferred state for strict-required scalars on create, never a silent bypass. A typed marker or a defer option with a reason (CLI and SDK create options), recorded in history; pm health and pm validate list deferred fields as curation work; strict close still requires concrete values so a deferral never lets incomplete work finish; optionally the deferral is allowed only for items with external provenance or for callers that declare an import capability.

Strict create accepts an explicit deferral for deadline, assignee and acceptance criteria with a reason, through the CLI and the SDK create options; The deferral is recorded in history and pm validate and pm health list deferred fields as curation work; Strict close still requires concrete values for every deferred field; A strict-preset importer run creates items without inventing values and the pm-github sync no longer rolls back
An importer creates a strict item with explicitly deferred fields
Strict create refuses every unknown deadline, assignee or acceptance criteria
